clue.text: Consumer guide for this week — see intervening answers

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a buyer's handbook or magazine guide for the coming week
setter's reading: the other answers in the grid are festive things to buy, a list a shopper takes out in late December

explanation.surface: A shopper's guide to this week's buys, with a pointer to the rest of the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The other answers (mince pies, turkey, crackers, candles, champagne and so on) are the items on the list, which is why the clue points to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A written list of goods a consumer intends to buy guides them round the shops in the festive week.

clue.text: Something needed in court, always reduced for crook

indicators.note: something reduced has been cut down, here losing one of its middle letters as in a poetic contraction

parts.note: a racket is needed on a tennis or squash court
ever means always

explanation.surface: Something essential in a courtroom is always cut back for the sake of a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, which fits 'crook', but it is a tennis court. EVER without its V is the poetic E'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer is a criminal who runs a fraudulent or extortionate business, so a crook.

clue.text: Helper on course scoundrel gets pass on

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: A rogue on a golf course is handed a pass by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's clubs and advises them, an assistant on the golf course.

clue.text: In relation to benefit, including right to claim again

parts.note: re means concerning or in relation to

indicators.note: one word including another holds it inside its own letters

parts.note: an asset is a benefit or advantage
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A welfare claimant makes a fresh claim to a benefit they have a right to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Benefit' reads as a welfare payment but means an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassert something is to state or insist on it once more, making the same claim a second time.

clue.text: Announced total, approximately

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: a sum is a total

explanation.surface: An estimated figure is given out as a rough total.
explanation.definitionFit: Some can mean roughly before a number, as in 'some fifty people', an approximation.

clue.text: Give authority to soldier before scheduled meeting

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second in the finished word

parts.note: a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: An officer authorises a soldier ahead of an arranged meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To mandate is to empower or officially instruct, granting someone authority to act.

clue.text: Name of female appearing in revised issue

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so its letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman's name turns up in the new edition of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a girl's given name, a familiar form of Susan.

clue.text: Male American fliers in ancient jumbos

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
Am is the abbreviation for American
moths are flying insects

explanation.surface: American men flying in old jumbo jets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbos' suggests jumbo jets beside 'fliers', but it means elephants.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoths were huge prehistoric elephants, and jumbo is an informal word for an elephant.

clue.text: Part of what one regrets as person making amends

indicators.note: part of a phrase means a run of consecutive letters taken from inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Some of what a person regrets marks them out as someone putting things right.
explanation.definitionFit: One who atones seeks to make up for a wrong, a repentant person making amends.

clue.text: Remedy for overindulgence I can't set out in advertisement

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the outer word

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement

indicators.note: to set out things is to lay them in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An advert for a hangover cure that can't quite describe itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid neutralises stomach acid, relieving the indigestion that follows eating too much.

clue.text: Cookie ingredients old man's mixed

indicators.note: mixed ingredients are stirred together, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Grandad's biscuit ingredients have been stirred together.
explanation.definitionFit: Almonds are nuts often baked into biscuits, so they are things a cookie recipe uses.

clue.text: Strange specimen I provided for baked goods

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so these letters come out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd sample I supplied for the bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: Mince pies are small British sweet pastries filled with dried fruit and spices, eaten at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Mince pies are pastries made in the oven, so they are baked goods.

clue.text: Sponge, say, a piece of which isn't hard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sponge is one kind of this baked dessert

definitions.text: a piece of which isn't hard
definitions.meaning: second meaning: from the idiom 'a piece of ___' for an easy task

explanation.walkthrough: 'Isn't hard' looks like a comment on texture, but it is the idiom: a task described as a piece of this is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is an example of the dessert, and the idiom 'piece of ___' means something simple.

clue.text: Fare for holiday in foreign country

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the bird roasted for Christmas dinner
second meaning: the nation spanning Europe and Asia

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare for holiday' reads like the price of a trip abroad, but fare here is food.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the traditional festive meal, and the same word names the nation whose capital is Ankara.

clue.text: Sources of party hats and nuts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Christmas novelties pulled apart with a bang, each holding a paper hat

explanation.surface: Where the party hats and the nuts come from at a festive meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Christmas crackers are British party favours: a paper tube two people pull until it snaps, releasing a paper crown and a trinket. 'Nuts' suggests food but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers hold paper crowns, and as an adjective the word is British slang for insane.

clue.text: Quality of some snacks princess ordered second

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new sequence, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A princess orders a second helping of crunchy snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisps and crackers are prized for a dry crunchiness, the snap you hear on biting.

clue.text: State of uncertainty that gives us power in hearing, say

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: hearing is an example of one of the five faculties
taken as written
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A tense wait gives the court power at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests a court session, but with 'say' it is an example of a bodily faculty.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is anxious uncertainty while waiting to learn how something turns out.

clue.text: Erects barrier around someone aiding criminal offence

parts.note: a fence is a receiver who sells stolen goods for thieves
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone builds a wall round an accomplice who helped with a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a fence sin: the receiver's own offence, the two pieces simply joined.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose a space with a paling or wall is to shut it in with a barrier.

clue.text: Starts covering up blunder making fortified wines

indicators.note: covering up something means wrapping it so it sits inside

parts.note: shies means starts or jumps aside in fright, as a horse does
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone begins hiding a mistake while making strong wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' looks like an indicator for first letters, but it is a verb meaning jumps in alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is wine from Jerez strengthened with added brandy, making it a fortified wine.

clue.text: Gradually consume some treat, intoxicated

indicators.note: some of a phrase is a portion lifted from inside its letters

parts.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Slowly eat part of a treat while drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into savings or time is to use them up bit by bit, consuming them gradually.

clue.text: Cuban products leaders of Irish government put in vehicles

indicators.note: put in means placed inside another word

parts.note: cars are vehicles

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letters are used

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Cuban goods given to Irish ministers as official cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana cigars are among Cuba's most famous exports, rolled tobacco products.

clue.text: Imposing latest period to avoid oysters?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: majestic, venerable, inspiring awe
second meaning: by tradition oysters are eaten only in months with an R, so this is the last month without one

explanation.walkthrough: The old rule says eat oysters only when the month's name has an R; the run of R-less months from May ends with this one, then September begins.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means grand and dignified, and as a noun it is the eighth month.

clue.text: Gift container king put in odd place

indicators.note: put in places one letter inside another word
odd means peculiar, so the word is jumbled into a peculiar order

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is placed in a strange spot as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped package, a container in which a present is posted or given.

clue.text: Spread put on 15 or loaf

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a savoury paste spread on the biscuits of 15-across
second meaning: loaf is slang for the head, as is this word

explanation.walkthrough: Loaf means head from rhyming slang (loaf of bread, head), and pate is an old word for the top of the head. '15' points to crackers as biscuits, not the party novelties.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a paste of meat or fish spread on biscuits, and pate is the crown of the skull.

clue.text: Call for peace expressed in lots of cards

indicators.note: expressed means put into speech, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: pax, Latin for peace, is a cry for a truce in British school games

explanation.surface: An appeal for peace is spoken while dealing hands of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack is a full deck of playing cards, so several packs are lots of cards.

clue.text: Feigned suffering, we hear, resulting in celebratory drink

indicators.note: we hear marks the words as heard rather than read, so it is their sound that matters

parts.note: sham means feigned and pain means suffering

explanation.surface: Pretending to be hurt earns someone a glass of bubbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkling wine from the French region is the traditional drink for toasting a celebration.

clue.text: Fellow adding sauce in alcoholic drink with egg

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
sauce and lip both mean cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A man pours a sauce into an eggnog-style drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks culinary next to drink and egg, but it means impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: A flip is a mixed drink of spirit or wine beaten with egg and sugar.

clue.text: Tree decorations also found in non-U things like this

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside another word
non- means without, so the word that follows loses that letter

parts.note: the reader is looking at one of these right now
and means also

explanation.surface: Christmas tree ornaments are also among things not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper-class, which hides the letter to be dropped. Candles were once fixed to Christmas tree branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Small candles clipped to branches were the traditional way of lighting and decorating a Christmas tree.

clue.text: Important people in Leicester and Derby, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: big shots, from the slang 'big cheese'
second meaning: Red Leicester and Derby are English varieties of a dairy food

explanation.walkthrough: Leicester and Derby look like English cities; here they are the cheeses named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Big cheeses are bosses in slang, and Leicester and Derby are named dairy products made from curdled milk.
